facts.fact: Rest of World reports Galaxy Backbone, a government-established company, runs two data centres in Abuja and Kano and provides core cloud services to government agencies and private companies (dated to the article, 2025-02-25, which gives no opening date).

Rest of World describes Galaxy Backbone as a privately held company established by the Nigerian government, which provides cloud services to government agencies and private companies and runs two data centres, one in Abuja and one in Kano; the article gives no further ownership detail.

Rest of World lists Suburban Cloud, an Abuja-based cloud provider founded by Bruce Ayonote, among homegrown Nigerian cloud companies, and says it has an Abuja data centre; the article gives no ownership detail beyond that and the date is the article's publication date.

Rest of World states that AWS (Amazon Web Services) opened a small local zone centre in Lagos in 2023 and that no other global cloud company has a data centre in Nigeria; the date given is the opening year.

systems.system: Layer3 cloud (colocated in two Lagos and one Abuja data centres)

systems.owner: Galaxy Backbone, privately held, established by the Nigerian government

note: carried from datacentres; no document opened
